XCAPITOLO.Corpo:
Legend of the degree of reliability

* low level : Detection of the car repairer, case study of the fault not found by the manufacturer.

** medium level : Extensive fault history, found by service technicians and repairers.

*** high level : Certainty of the fault, good degree of "repetition" reported by the manufacturer.

• System: Injection

  • Device: - -

  • Fault: The engine fault, Start&Stop and generic fault warning lights come on intermittently from time to time. The message ‘Start&Stop not available’ appears on the instrument cluster display, whilst the car continues to operate correctly.

  • Faults detected by the self-diagnostic system: One or more of the following:
    • P0300 (Misfire in unspecified cylinders – Fault)
    • P0301 (Misfire in cylinder 1 – Fault)
    • P0304 (Misfire, cylinder 4 – Fault)
  • Cause: Incorrect injection parameter settings – Tachometer

• Procedure: Using diagnostic equipment, carry out the following procedures: “cam profile reset”, “auto-adaptive parameter reset” and “tachometer wheel reset”, followed by the relevant calibration.

  • Procedure: Calibration of the phonic wheel is carried out as follows:
    • Bring the engine up to operating temperature.
    • Accelerate to 5000 rpm and maintain this speed for approximately 2 seconds
    • Leave the engine idling for a further 2 seconds
    • Repeat the acceleration sequence until the engine fault warning light goes out
    • The warning light usually goes out after the third repetition
  • Note: During an initial service, the spark plugs, the coil (the vehicle is fitted with a single coil) and the timing kit were replaced, but this did not resolve the fault. Only after carrying out the “cam profile reset”, “self-adaptive parameter reset”, “tachometer wheel reset” and the subsequent calibration phase was the problem fully resolved,
    In this particular case, the engine warning light came on after the tachometer wheel reset. The calibration procedure was then carried out to definitively resolve the fault, resulting in the warning light going out.
